narrative:
On October 27, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 48.7%, addressing 1,423 of 2,923 scheduled matters across 45 benches. This marks a notable efficiency gain compared to mid-October benchmarks, when daily hearing rates stood at 40.1% on October 16, 38.8% on October 15, and 39.5% on October 14. Total hearings completed increased by roughly 200 cases despite a consistent scheduling volume.

Bench throughput exhibited significant divergence. Justice S Rachaiah managed the heaviest docket in Hall 30, hearing 96 of 153 listed cases (62.7%). High clearance rates were also registered by Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar in Hall 22 (72 of 105 heard, 68.6%) and Justice T.P. Vivekananda in Hall 36 (43 of 53 heard, 81.1%). Conversely, certain rosters experienced severe bottlenecks: Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum heard 9 of 81 matters (11.1%) in Hall 14, while a 95-case docket under Justice C.M. Poonacha in Hall 31 saw only 1 matter heard (1.1%).

By procedural stage, interlocutory Orders formed the bulk of scheduled business, converting at 53.3% (576 of 1,081 heard), alongside Preliminary Hearings at 53.4%. Although Final Hearings converted at a lower rate of 31.9% (152 of 476 heard), this demonstrated steady recovery compared to mid-October figures (ranging between 20.2% and 30.3%). 

Writ Petitions constituted nearly half the court's listings with 1,362 scheduled matters; their hearing rate reached 45.2%, improving markedly from the 34% to 36% rates recorded on prior days. Criminal Petitions (55.3%) and Miscellaneous First Appeals (56.6%) demonstrated steady clearance, whereas Regular Second Appeals lagged behind at a conversion rate of just 16.2%.
